## 開篇固定收益主論述

投資人持續降低對聯準會即將升息的預期，卻要求更高報酬才願意承接長天期政府與公司融資，使美國公債殖利率曲線在8月17日進一步陡峭化。30年期殖利率上升4.7個基點至5.308%，創2007年以來新高；10年期上升3個基點至4.723%，2年期則僅升0.6個基點至4.177%。因此，2s30s擴大4.1個基點至113.1個基點，2s10s擴大2.4個基點至54.6個基點。

本次走勢的組成格外清楚。10年期實質殖利率上升2.8個基點至2.438%，幾乎解釋名目殖利率的全部漲幅；10年期損益兩平通膨率僅升0.2個基點至2.285%。油價重新上漲，意味通膨風險仍在，但更直接的壓力來自實質借款成本，以及投資人持有長天期債券所要求的溢價，而不是市場全面重估預期通膨。

這項負擔愈來愈難與人工智慧投資週期分開看待。週一12筆交易再增加$91億發行量後，美國8月投資級債發行額已達$1,452億，創歷年同月紀錄。今年高評級債券發行額接近$1.5兆，其中最大型科技公司約占$2,000億。投資人與策略師日益認為，這些供給正與美國公債直接競逐同一批長天期資金。

問題不只在於公司債發行量創紀錄。科技公司與資料中心計畫相較政府債券提供大幅讓利，鼓勵投資人透過減持美國公債，挪出部分資金投入AI基礎建設。野村估計，超大規模雲端業者今年的借款，相當於美國財政部對民間投資人發行之中長期公債淨額約25%，占比是2025年的5倍。美國銀行經濟學家則估計，公司債與不動產抵押貸款證券發行量合計增加，已在2026年推高10年期殖利率約30個基點。

聯邦政府借款仍是更大的結構性力量。年度赤字接近$2兆，上週30年期公債標售殖利率須達5.216%才能完成，為2001年以來同類標售最高水準。不過，財政部大量倚重國庫券，並維持10年期與30年期標售規模不變，使中長期公債預估淨供給較2025年減少約$4,400億。公司債市場不僅補足這項減量，供給更有過之：巴克萊預期公司債淨供給將增加$4,740億，其中很大一部分與科技建設有關。

美國與伊朗達成協議的前景轉差，也讓油價對長天期債券構成額外挑戰。美國總統川普表示，不打算延長6月簽署、原本設有60天談判期的備忘錄，黎巴嫩戰事也再度升溫。WTI上漲3.05%至$84.91，布蘭特原油上漲2.94%至$91.12。原油透過荷莫茲海峽的替代轉運方式，迄今有助於限制實體供應受阻的程度；然而，外交協議未獲延長，代表市場仍缺乏一套能長久規範這條運輸路線的安排。

因此，本交易日延續的是聯準會政策路徑與殖利率曲線長端的分歧，而非逆轉較溫和的政策展望。就業、零售銷售與通膨數據轉弱後，高盛首席經濟學家Jan Hatzius認為9月升息的可能性非常低。交易員一週前才完全反映12月升息，如今已把下次升息25個基點的預期時點推遲至1月。美元指數下跌0.13%，來到5月以來最弱區域；黃金期貨則上漲2.25%至$4,479.10。

風險性資產並未把聯準會升息預期降溫視為全然利多。市場持續看好AI需求，費城半導體指數上漲1.64%，但標普500指數下跌0.52%，那斯達克100指數下跌0.17%，VIX則上升6.60%至15.19。這組走勢反映投資人的兩難：AI資本支出週期仍支撐推動這波投資的企業，但為此所需的融資也加重殖利率壓力，拖累其他資產。

## 長天期供給壓過較溫和的聯準會路徑

美國公債賣壓集中在融資與期限溢價風險最顯著的曲線區段。5年期殖利率上升1個基點至4.375%，遠低於30年期的4.7個基點升幅。過去一個月，2年期幾乎持平、微降0.3個基點，10年期卻上升17.4個基點，30年期更上升23.7個基點；同期2s30s陡峭化24個基點。

長天期債券報酬也呈現相同分化。到期年限至少20年的美國公債指數週一下跌0.77%，一個月跌幅達3.29%；到期年限超過20年的美國高品質公司債當日下跌0.76%，長天期BBB債下跌0.69%。這些市場一方面承受政府債券基準殖利率上升，另一方面也要消化與其競逐投資人資金的新增長天期公司債。

邊際美債買家對價格日益敏感，使供給壓力更具影響力。外國官方機構過去持有美國債務，部分是為了管理外匯存底；如今，民間基金、交易商與槓桿投資人會把美國公債和日益擴大的替代投資選項相互比較。本月稍早發行的一檔Alphabet 30年期債券殖利率接近6.4%，比相近天期政府債券高約1.15個百分點；上月一筆與Meta相關的資料中心融資，支付的殖利率更超過7.5%。

Morningstar資料顯示，這種相對價值促使投資級債券基金減持美國公債，並把公司債平均配置比重提高至30%，創3年新高。這項轉變不一定代表投資人對政府債務失去信心，卻意味美國公債必須提供足以與高評級公司債競爭的殖利率；後者不僅有可觀利差，有些還有資料中心長期租約所提供的合約現金流。

週一的次級市場活動，與殖利率曲線最長端出現顯著調整的情況一致。剩餘到期年限超過20年的附息名目美國公債，以原始面額計算的交易量達$1,344億，比週五增加15.1%；交易商與客戶間的交易占54%。這些數據無法判斷客戶交易方向，卻顯示長端殖利率上升時成交量同步增加，並非發生在交投冷清的市場。

Citadel Securities則從政策角度解釋長端走勢。該公司歐洲、中東及非洲固定收益銷售主管Nohshad Shah表示，通膨多年高於目標後，投資人懷疑貨幣與財政當局是否願意作出艱難抉擇，因此長期殖利率仍接近20年高點。他指出，超過55%的核心商品價格仍在上漲，並認為9月決策勢均力敵，判斷比高盛更偏鷹派。

投資人尚無須先判定兩種看法何者正確，當日市場走勢已清楚反映兩股力量的分化。市場降低對聯準會2026年升息的預期，帶動美元走弱，也限制2年期殖利率升幅；長債則同時面對赤字、油價不確定性與新增民間供給。若通膨再度加速，賣壓最終可能延伸至曲線前端；但週一損益兩平通膨率幾乎未變，顯示當日曲線陡峭化主要由實質殖利率與融資壓力驅動。

## AI借款再創初級市場紀錄

繼6月與7月先後創新高後，8月成為美國投資級債連續第3個發行量創紀錄的月份。截至週一，發行額達$1,452億，超越2020年創下的原8月紀錄$1,360億。今年迄今發行量達$1.46兆，比2020年同期高8.5%；當年疫情緊急借款曾締造全年發行紀錄。

Alphabet本月發行$250億美元債，是最大貢獻者，也是2026年第8筆規模至少達此水準的科技業交易。摩根大通把科技、媒體與電信公司全年債券發行預測上調約20%至$5,400億。供給可能持續偏向長天期：到期年限超過10年的債券占投資級發行比重，已從2025年的13%升至20%，相當於增加約$1,900億長天期債券。

部分估算顯示，其整體影響已可與美國公債供給相比。巴克萊指出，新增長天期公司債發行量，相當於30年期美國公債全年$2,760億發行額的近70%。AI支出結合收購融資與再融資需求後，2026年投資級借款總額預計接近$2兆。

市場仍願意提供資金，但買方變得更挑剔。上週發行人收緊定價時，投資人平均撤回約36%的高評級債初始訂單，顯示市場對讓利不足的交易容忍度降低。這股抵制並未阻止週一發行量再創紀錄，卻影響個別借款人對發行規模與定價的拿捏。

私募信貸業者發債同樣獲得充沛需求。Blackstone Private Credit Fund原先設定約$5億的5年期債券發行目標，在訂單一度接近$20億後，把規模擴大至$7.5億。該債券以美國公債加碼2.05個百分點定價，比初步討論水準收窄約25個基點。

Blue Owl Technology Finance的一筆增額發行最高取得$10.5億訂單，因此把目標規模倍增至$4億。債券最終以2.5個百分點利差定價，低於既有債券初次發行時的2.65個百分點。這些結果顯示，近期市場雖擔憂軟體相關私募信貸的估值，部分基金贖回也受到限制，但成熟管理人的公開債券融資管道並未因此關閉。

投資人也對結構更複雜的AI曝險展現興趣。名為Project Odyssey、與微軟相關的資料中心融資取得超過$80億需求，規模可能增至$39億，比最初構想高約$10億。這批預計取得投資級評等的5年期債券，行銷票息位於6%區間高端，並以折價發行，使殖利率落在7%區間低端至中段，更接近單B級垃圾債，而非傳統高評級債券。

債券將由黑石支持的QTS Realty Trust旗下子公司發行，用於資助喬治亞州一項資料中心計畫。超大規模雲端業者簽訂的長期租約，可支撐投資級待遇；但即使最終承租人是微軟，擬議殖利率仍顯示投資人要求針對專案結構、施工與集中度風險獲得補償。交易最快可能於週二進入市場，但仍可能有變。

Alphabet也正把融資計畫擴展到更多幣別。公司準備首次發行澳幣債券，目標規模約A$50億，分為4個到期年限，最長達20年。今年Alphabet已發行美元、瑞士法郎、英鎊、歐元、加幣與日圓債券，另有近$850億股權發行；公司對2026年的資本支出預測已提高至最高$2,050億。

澳洲市場既能提供在地分散效果，科技業發行人也相對稀少。即使全球投資人已對超大規模雲端業者的龐大借款量顯露疲態，這些特點仍可支撐需求。兩者的差別很重要：創紀錄月份過後，買方可能拒絕另一筆定價偏緊的美元券，卻願意接受能填補當地投資組合缺口的首次發行人。

AI融資週期並非只透過債券供給影響美國公債殖利率。即使其他經濟領域轉弱，資料中心、晶片、電力與人力支出仍支撐成長。摩根大通策略師預期，到2030年為止，基礎建設支出總額將達$5.5兆。這類投資可藉由強化需求維持實質利率高檔；與之相伴的借款，也會吸收政府為赤字融資所需的同一批資金。

## 日本GDP疲弱仍未阻止公債重挫

日本第2季經濟成長不如預期，政府公債仍遭拋售，顯示市場研判近期政策時，匯率壓力、通膨與財政不確定性依舊比內需疲弱更具分量。10年期日本公債殖利率一度上升5.5個基點至2.93%，創1996年以來新高；20年期上升6.5個基點至3.815%，30年期上升6個基點至4.07%，逼近5月紀錄。

第2季實質GDP折合年率成長1.1%，低於2%的預測中位數，也較前季修正後的1.9%放緩，但經濟仍連續第3季成長。內需項目尤其疲弱，而這些正是日本央行判斷需求能否承受較高利率時通常會檢視的指標。

資本投資較前季下降1.2%（未年化），不僅不如經濟學家預期的成長0.5%，跌幅也大於第1季修正後的1%。生活成本上升抑制家庭支出，民間消費持平，未達0.4%的預估增幅。這項結果與強勁的企業調查及工業生產形成對比，凸顯樂觀的企業信心與實際支出之間仍有落差。

通膨正是這項分歧的核心。7月企業物價較上年同期上漲7.2%，企業把燃料、原料與進口成本轉嫁給客戶的壓力升高。荷莫茲海峽實際上仍未恢復正常通行，日本已分散原油採購來源；美國6月占日本原油進口量近三分之一，高於2月的7%。日圓疲弱則進一步放大這些外部成本。

GDP公布後，日圓約報159兌1美元，仍遠弱於126.09的10年平均值，且接近7月底促使美日協調干預的水準。隔夜交換市場反映日本央行在9月18日會議升息的機率約80%。據知情人士透露，首相高市早苗政府支持在9月或10月升息。

GDP疲弱使升息理由更難說明。消費持平、企業投資萎縮之際，9月升息很難被描述為因應經濟過熱，反而可能主要被視為支撐日圓、限制輸入型通膨。這並不排除日本央行採取行動，卻會改變投資人對本輪緊縮週期能否延續的解讀。

前日本高階外匯官員中尾武彥主張大幅加快腳步，認為日本央行應在每次會議升息，最終把政策利率提高至2%以上。他表示，在通膨約2%的情況下，2.25%或2.5%的利率並不異常；目前政策利率為1%，實質借款成本仍為負值。這項提議不是日本央行的政策指引，卻反映部分前外匯官員施加的壓力；他們認為貨幣政策有必要強化匯率干預效果。

財政政策也為長端帶來另一項風險。高市計畫自4月起，把食品消費稅降至1%，為期兩年，但政府尚未說明如何籌措財源。家庭減稅可在第2季成長疲弱後支撐消費；若未有財源配套，則會加深市場對公共債務負擔的憂慮，目前日本公債規模已超過經濟產值的兩倍。

日本公債賣壓也是全球政府債券重新定價的一部分。法國10年期殖利率維持在2009年以來最高點附近，德國殖利率約在2011年水準，加拿大30年期殖利率則創2010年以來新高。在32個交換市場中，有三分之二反映利率將上升；市場預期未來一年7個主要市場的升息幅度合計約400個基點。

全球情勢並非完全一致。日本必須權衡消費疲弱與匯率、進口物價壓力；歐洲面對能源與國防支出，美國則承受龐大的財政與公司長天期債券供給。共同結果是：當能源成本上升、財政擴張與AI投資同時發生，跨主權債市分散配置所能提供的保護便會降低。

## 新興市場的流動性與成長訊號分歧

印度儲備銀行宣布，將於8月底關閉提供海外居民的特殊美元存款窗口，比原定時程提早一個月，導致印度出現已開發市場以外最劇烈的主權債市反應。這項公告令交易員意外，因為總裁Sanjay Malhotra在8月5日政策會議上才排除提前終止的可能性。

5年期印度政府公債殖利率一度上升9個基點至6.44%，10年期上升4個基點至6.80%。這項存款機制已吸引超過$500億資金，相關流入使外匯存底在3週內增加逾$300億至$7,070億。提前關閉窗口，意味未來可用來支撐短天期債券的盧比流動性將會減少。

盧比貶值0.2%至95.58兌1美元。花旗把盧比短期可能升至的水準從94下修至95，並把該機制總流入預測下調$100億至$700億。該行認為，即使外匯存底增加讓決策者更有能力抑制波動，推動盧比大幅升值也不是印度儲備銀行的主要目標。

印度儲備銀行也可能認為，更多資金流入的邊際效益正在降低。這些存款天期為3至5年，會形成未來的外幣負債，央行還須負擔遠期溢價成本。不過，另兩項供銀行與國營企業使用的機制仍將開放至12月。

因此，印度銀行仍有誘因發行境外債券。金融機構今年已發行創紀錄的$80億美元債，超越2019年全年$79.2億的原紀錄。ICICI Bank週一正在行銷另一筆交易；Kotak Mahindra Bank與Yes Bank則已為可能發行的指標規模債券聘請顧問。

境外借款交換機制為銀行提供1.5%的固定年化避險成本，平均到期年限須至少3年，成本低於市場水準。印度企業今年的美元借款約有三分之二來自金融機構。即使眼前融資需求過後發行量可能放緩，存款計畫提前結束仍可能促使銀行在未來數週加快發債。

巴西呈現限制性政策的另一種結果。央行6月經濟活動指數較前月下降0.64%，跌幅超過經濟學家預期的0.5%，也是2025年5月以來最大萎縮。經濟活動仍較上年同期成長2.35%；數據顯示，第1季成長1.1%後，第2季經濟擴張0.2%。

巴西央行過去4次會議每次均調降Selic利率25個基點，使其降至14%，但尚未承諾9月繼續降息。工業生產、服務業與通膨轉弱，強化進一步寬鬆的理由；然而，通膨仍高於3%目標，財政政策也使長期預期維持高檔。

財政部長Dario Durigan坦言，投資人對強制性支出與公共債務走勢的憂慮有其道理，政府必須改善這一路徑。通膨預期直到2028年仍高於目標，即使當前經濟活動轉弱，也使寬鬆週期更難推進。Durigan未支持任何特定的退休金或支出規則結構改革，因此財政因應方案在10月選舉前仍懸而未決。

亞洲其他地區方面，泰國第2季經濟較上年同期成長1.9%，低於第1季的2.8%，但仍略高於1.8%的預測。民間投資成長13.4%，為2012年以來最大增幅；較高能源成本與旅遊受阻則拖累國內活動。政府上調全年成長預測區間的下限，使預估區間來到2%至2.5%，但家庭債務偏高與小型企業信用品質惡化仍是限制因素。

中國7月數據凸顯AI相關工業經濟與內需之間更明顯的分歧。工業生產較上年同期成長4.5%，零售銷售增幅放緩至0.6%，前7個月固定資產投資下降6.7%，全數低於預期。電子設備產出增加超過19%，仍不足以抵銷消費與投資更廣泛的放緩。

希臘則提供正面的財政對照。政府計畫於2026年提前償還約€130億債務，包括約€25億歐洲金融穩定機制貸款、一筆2027年到期的€22億債券，以及減少€12億國庫券。計畫尚未定案，但強勁的基本預算盈餘，加上預計年底前超過€300億的現金準備，使雅典有餘裕降低未來融資需求。

債務管理機構預期，希臘債務占GDP比率今年將降至137%，低於先前預估的138.2%。較快的降債進度，已協助希臘10年期殖利率低於義大利、法國與英國。這與美國、日本借款成本上升形成的對比，關鍵不在希臘債務的絕對規模，而在融資需求的變化方向，以及提前清償債務所建立的可信度。

## 公司融資管道暢通與借款人嚴重承壓並存

初級市場發行量創紀錄，仍未阻止個別信用債大幅重新定價。一篇報導檢視保險公司Sammons Financial Group與Guggenheim Partners及其執行長Mark Walter之間的關係後，Sammons於2036年6月到期的債券跌至發行以來最低水準。該債券相對基準的利差由一週前1.47個百分點擴大至約2個百分點。

報導發布機構揭露，旗下投資部門正放空這批債券，並引用申報文件，稱Sammons是Guggenheim的關係人。惠譽6月給予該保險公司A-評等，理由包括資本實力非常強勁，但對較高風險資產的曝險略為偏高。Sammons與Guggenheim均未回應。

檢察官與監管機關正在調查Walter旗下保險公司向其商業版圖其他部分提供的貸款；在此之際，Guggenheim自身債務狀況惡化，進一步加深市場疑慮。Guggenheim一筆2031年11月到期的第一順位有擔保定期貸款，週一報價低於面額每1美元80美分，低於7月20日約平價水準。相較高評級債與私募信貸基金發行需求普遍強勁，這項走勢凸顯特定借款人的信用風險。

巴西方面，Grupo Casas Bahia在2024年啟動的庭外重整未能穩定財務後，已聲請法院監督的破產保護。這家零售商列出的原因包括高利率、信用緊縮、融資成本上升、消費疲弱與營運資金壓力。公司股價一度重挫36%，創歷史新低。

當地媒體報導，公司負債達173億里亞爾。上半年營收為144億里亞爾，淨損較上年同期擴大18.4%至112億里亞爾。Casas Bahia為轉向獲利能力較佳的業務，已關閉298家門市並裁減人力，但原先規劃的籌措流動性替代方案未能實現。公司尋求延長債務期限期間，打算讓其餘銷售通路繼續營運。

Braskem另須在8月24日前達成庭外協議，否則也可能尋求類似的司法保護。Petrobras正考慮為這家石化生產商提供更有利的商業條件，包括延長付款期限、降低利率並增加石腦油供應。Petrobras占Braskem石腦油供應的比重已由最高70%降至約30%，迫使Braskem更加依賴其他供應商與銀行信貸。

目前尚未作成決定。國際債券持有人已提出Braskem與部分債權人認為更有利的條件，但公司須取得至少持有三分之一債務的債權人支持。部分債權人希望Petrobras提供股本、營運資金或次順位債務。這家國營控股石油公司不願注資，因為此舉可能提高其持股，並可能使Braskem的債務併入自身資產負債表。

印尼開發商Modernland Realty正嘗試第2次重整一筆明年4月到期、規模$2.745億的美元債。公司提議先把到期日延至2028年6月30日，最終再將債務交換為永續證券；後者由轉移至債權人控制載體的資產提供支持。

每$1,000本金的債券，持有人將先收到$50付款。修訂後債券將按年累計3%的以債付息（PIK）利息，重整生效前未支付的利息則轉為本金。部分擔保品將獲釋，使Modernland可把這些資產用於一筆新的$3,400萬融資。根據擬議的預先包裝式新加坡重整計畫，債權人須在8月24日前投票。

Riverside Military Academy在約$4,800萬市政債券違約後，取得較長喘息期。暫緩追索協議將持續至2027年8月31日，校方並將利用一筆次順位$800萬貸款，向債券持有人支付自2025年3月起漏付的款項。學生人數已由2019年的509人降至2024年的180人，減幅接近65%，削弱支撐債務的營運基礎。

這些案例顯示，市場融資管道暢通與信用修復是兩回事。高評級發行人與成熟私募信貸基金只要提供足夠利差，仍可擴大交易；承壓借款人則須依靠延長到期日、以債付息、次順位資本與法院保護。偏高的基準殖利率同時強化兩種結果：定價合理的優質新債可吸引資金，但營運已惡化的企業更難完成再融資。

## 後續市場意義

聯準會週三公布的7月會議紀要，將是檢驗政策預期與長期殖利率差距擴大的下一個關鍵。官員以9比3票決定維持利率不變，但紀要可能顯示，這項決定是否比票數所呈現的更為勉強，也可看出在最新偏弱的就業、零售銷售與物價報告公布前，決策者對商品價格漲勢持續的憂慮有多普遍。

若討論內容強調耐心，將支持高盛對9月不太可能升息的判斷，讓曲線長端主要依供給、財政政策與實質殖利率交易。若官員更憂慮超過半數核心商品價格仍在上漲，則會強化Citadel認為9月決策勢均力敵的看法，並可能使2年期更全面加入賣壓。

30年期殖利率創本輪週期新高後，本週20年期美國公債標售將直接檢驗需求。公司借款人正提供可觀利差，投資級發行日程也相當密集，關鍵在於最新殖利率讓利能否吸引持久買盤。若標售結果疲弱，殖利率曲線陡峭化將再添一項供給訊號；若得標結果強勁、次級市場交易穩定，則顯示5%以上殖利率已開始吸引長天期資金。

油價仍是最迫切的通膨風險。川普拒絕延長與伊朗的協議，加上黎巴嫩戰事重啟，把布蘭特油價推升至$91以上；但生產商仍透過荷莫茲海峽周邊的替代轉運方式運送原油。即使沒有外交解決方案，只要運量維持、運費或保險成本下降，經濟影響仍可受控。若轉運受阻、伊朗港口周邊執法收緊或攻擊加劇，能源價格上升進入通膨預期及央行政策定價的風險就會提高。

英國週三公布的通膨率預計較上年同期上升2.9%，將是4個月來首次加速。能源帳單、航空旅行，以及AI相關電子零組件短缺，預計均會帶來影響。數據將檢驗英國央行能否把進口與特定產業的價格壓力，和更廣泛的國內通膨動能區分開來。

日本、中國、泰國與巴西先後公布較弱數據後，週五的全球採購經理人調查將是下一項廣泛的經濟活動檢驗。美國數據若強勁到足以維持其成長優勢，可能推動美元反彈，使市場更難繼續降低聯準會升息押注。若數據進一步轉弱，將強化曲線前端對聯準會保持耐心的定價；不過，只要公司借款與財政供給仍重，長端殖利率未必隨之下降。

日本央行9月18日會議如今面對更棘手的證據組合。市場反映約80%的升息機率、日圓接近159，以及企業物價上漲7.2%，均支持採取行動；但GDP折合年率僅成長1.1%、消費持平及投資下降，則不利於展開積極的連續升息。日本央行的指引若能釐清，升息一次只是為了穩定匯率，還是代表加快正常化的起點，其重要性至少不亞於升息本身。

初級信用市場也即將面對交易執行考驗。Project Odyssey最快可能於週二推出擴大後的微軟相關融資；Alphabet則預計先為4券次澳幣首發提供定價指引，並可能在隔日定價。完成這些交易所需的讓利，將顯示當地貨幣市場的稀缺性與專案的高殖利率，能否克服近期美國市場訂單流失所反映的疲態。

Modernland與Braskem均面臨8月24日期限，但市場要檢驗的是另一類問題。Modernland須為重整方案取得批准，以到期日展延與新的擔保品運用彈性，換取以債付息及最終發行永續證券。Braskem須取得至少三分之一債權人的支持，同時確認Petrobras能否在不承擔更大資產負債表義務的情況下提供商業紓困。兩案真正的市場考驗，都是新增資金、擔保品與損失如何分配，而不只是談判是否繼續。

overall_summary.headline: 財政與創紀錄AI借款壓過較溫和的聯準會路徑，美債曲線陡峭化
overall_summary.session_narrative:
市場降低聯準會近期升息預期，但長天期融資壓力更大，帶動美國公債殖利率曲線陡峭化。30年期殖利率上升4.7個基點至5.308%，創2007年以來新高；10年期上升3個基點至4.723%，2年期則僅升0.6個基點。10年期實質殖利率上升2.8個基點，幾乎解釋名目殖利率的全部漲幅；損益兩平通膨率僅升0.2個基點。

8月投資級債發行額達創紀錄的$1,452億；在市場原已必須為近$2兆的年度聯邦赤字提供融資之際，AI投資又增添長天期公司債供給。科技業借款人今年已發行約$2,000億債券，這些債券相對政府債券提供的讓利，正鼓勵投資人把資金從美國公債轉向公司債。美國與伊朗的談判期未獲延長，增加油價帶來的通膨風險；不過，荷莫茲海峽周邊的替代轉運仍持續限制實體供應中斷程度。

就業、零售銷售與通膨數據轉弱，使市場把聯準會下次升息的預期時點推遲至1月，壓低美元，也限制曲線前端賣壓。風險性資產表現仍分歧：AI需求推升半導體股，但這波投資週期所需的融資壓力抑制其他資產表現，導致大盤下跌、波動率上升。
overall_summary.summary: 赤字、龐大的AI相關公司債發行與油價風險再起推高長天期融資成本，使長天期美債殖利率上升、曲線陡峭化；較弱數據則把下次聯準會升息預期推遲至1月，令2年期殖利率升幅有限。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

The US Treasury curve steepened on Aug. 17 as investors continued to retreat from an imminent Federal Reserve increase while demanding still more compensation to finance long-dated government and corporate borrowing. The 30-year yield rose 4.7 basis points to 5.308%, its highest level since 2007, while the 10-year climbed 3 basis points to 4.723%. The 2-year increased just 0.6 basis point to 4.177%, widening 2s30s by 4.1 basis points to 113.1 basis points and 2s10s by 2.4 basis points to 54.6 basis points.

The composition made the distinction unusually clear. The 10-year real yield rose 2.8 basis points to 2.438%, accounting for nearly all the nominal move, while the 10-year breakeven increased only 0.2 basis point to 2.285%. Oil’s renewed advance preserved inflation risk, but the more immediate pressure came through real borrowing costs and the premium required to hold duration rather than a broad repricing of expected inflation.

That burden has become harder to separate from the artificial-intelligence investment cycle. US investment-grade issuance reached $145.2 billion for August, already a record for the month, after Monday’s 12 deals added another $9.1 billion. Almost $1.5 trillion of high-grade debt has been sold this year, with the biggest technology companies accounting for roughly $200 billion. Investors and strategists increasingly see that supply competing directly with Treasuries for the same long-duration capital.

The competition is not simply a matter of record corporate volume. Tech companies and data-center ventures are offering large concessions over government bonds, encouraging investors to finance AI infrastructure partly by reducing Treasury holdings. Nomura estimates hyperscaler borrowing this year is equivalent to roughly 25% of net Treasury note and bond issuance to private investors, five times the 2025 share. Bank of America economists estimate the combined increase in corporate and mortgage-backed issuance has added about 30 basis points to the 10-year yield during 2026.

Federal borrowing remains the larger structural force. Annual deficits are running near $2 trillion, and last week’s 30-year auction required a 5.216% yield, the highest for such a sale since 2001. Yet Treasury has leaned heavily on bills and kept its 10- and 30-year auction sizes steady, reducing projected net note and bond supply by about $440 billion from 2025. The corporate market has more than filled that reduction: Barclays expects net corporate supply to rise by $474 billion, much of it associated with the technology buildout.

Oil supplied an additional challenge to duration after prospects for a US-Iran agreement deteriorated. President Donald Trump said he did not intend to extend the June memorandum that had created a 60-day negotiating window, while fighting in Lebanon flared again. WTI rose 3.05% to $84.91 and Brent gained 2.94% to $91.12. Alternative crude transfers through the Strait of Hormuz have helped limit the physical disruption, but the failure to extend the diplomatic agreement left markets with no durable settlement governing the route.

The session therefore extended the separation between the Fed path and the long end rather than reversing the softer policy outlook. Goldman Sachs chief economist Jan Hatzius described a September increase as very unlikely after weaker employment, retail sales and inflation data. Traders shifted the expected timing of the next quarter-point move to January after fully pricing a December increase only a week earlier. The dollar index fell 0.13% to its weakest region since May, while gold futures rose 2.25% to $4,479.10.

Risk assets did not treat the lower expected Fed path as an unqualified benefit. The S&P 500 lost 0.52%, even as the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index gained 1.64% on continuing enthusiasm for AI demand. The Nasdaq 100 declined 0.17%, and the VIX rose 6.60% to 15.19. The combination captured the tension confronting investors: enthusiasm for the AI capital cycle continued to support the companies driving it, while the financing required for that cycle added to the yield pressure weighing on other assets.

## Long-Duration Supply Overrides the Softer Fed Path

The Treasury selloff was concentrated where financing and term-premium risks matter most. The 5-year yield rose 1 basis point to 4.375%, compared with the 4.7-basis-point increase in the 30-year. Over one month, the 2-year was almost unchanged, down 0.3 basis point, while the 10-year had risen 17.4 basis points and the 30-year 23.7 basis points. The 2s30s curve steepened 24 basis points over that period.

Long-duration bond returns reflected the same divide. An index of Treasuries with maturities of at least 20 years fell 0.77% Monday and was down 3.29% over one month. High-quality US corporate bonds with maturities beyond 20 years lost 0.76% on the day, and long BBB debt declined 0.69%. Those markets were absorbing a rise in their government benchmark alongside the new corporate duration competing for investor capital.

The supply pressure has become more consequential because the marginal Treasury buyer is increasingly price-sensitive. Foreign official institutions once accumulated US debt partly for reserve management, while private funds, dealers and leveraged investors weigh Treasuries against a widening set of alternatives. A 30-year Alphabet bond sold earlier in the month yielded nearly 6.4%, about 1.15 percentage points more than comparable government debt. A Meta-linked data-center financing issued last month paid more than 7.5%.

That relative value has prompted investment-grade bond funds to reduce Treasury holdings and lift average corporate allocations to 30%, the highest in three years, according to Morningstar. The shift need not represent a loss of confidence in government debt. It does mean Treasury must clear at yields attractive relative to highly rated corporate paper carrying substantial spread and, in some cases, contractual cash flow from long data-center leases.

Monday’s secondary-market activity was consistent with a significant adjustment at the far end. Trading in nominal Treasury coupons with more than 20 years to maturity reached $134.4 billion in original-face value, 15.1% more than Friday. Dealer-to-customer transactions accounted for 54% of that activity. The figures do not identify the direction of customer trades, but they show that the rise in long yields occurred alongside heavier turnover rather than in an inactive market.

Citadel Securities offered a more policy-centered explanation for the long end. Nohshad Shah, the firm’s head of EMEA fixed-income sales, argued that long yields remain near two-decade highs because investors doubt the willingness of monetary and fiscal authorities to make difficult choices after inflation has exceeded target for years. He noted that more than 55% of core goods prices were still rising and described September as a close decision, a more hawkish judgment than Goldman’s.

The completed market move did not require investors to resolve that disagreement. Reduced expectations for a 2026 Fed increase supported the dollar decline and limited the rise in the 2-year, while the long bond faced deficits, oil uncertainty and additional private supply. A renewed inflation acceleration could eventually pull the front end into the selloff, but Monday’s nearly unchanged breakeven showed that this session’s steepening was primarily a real-yield and financing event.

## AI Borrowing Sets Another Primary-Market Record

August became the third consecutive record month for US investment-grade issuance, following new highs in June and July. The $145.2 billion sold through Monday exceeded the previous August record of $136 billion set in 2020. Year-to-date issuance reached $1.46 trillion, 8.5% above the comparable point in 2020, when emergency pandemic borrowing produced the full-year record.

Alphabet’s $25 billion US dollar offering was the largest contributor this month and the eighth technology deal of at least that size in 2026. JPMorgan raised its forecast for annual bond issuance by technology, media and telecommunications companies by about 20% to $540 billion. The supply is likely to remain long-dated: the share of investment-grade issuance with maturities beyond 10 years has risen to 20% from 13% in 2025, representing about $190 billion of additional long-duration paper.

Some estimates put the broader effect in terms comparable with Treasury supply itself. The extra long corporate issuance is equivalent to almost 70% of the $276 billion in annual 30-year Treasury issuance, according to Barclays. Nearly $2 trillion of total investment-grade borrowing is expected in 2026 as AI spending combines with acquisition financing and refinancing needs.

The market is still providing that capital, though buyers are becoming more discriminating. Investors withdrew about 36% of initial high-grade orders on average during the previous week when issuers tightened pricing, revealing less tolerance for deals that offered insufficient concession. That pushback did not prevent Monday’s record, but it changed how individual borrowers approached size and price.

Private-credit vehicles found ample demand. Blackstone Private Credit Fund increased a 5-year bond sale to $750 million from an initial target of about $500 million after orders peaked near $2 billion. The note priced at a spread of 2.05 percentage points over Treasuries, roughly 25 basis points tighter than initial discussion.

Blue Owl Technology Finance doubled the targeted size of a reopening to $400 million after attracting as much as $1.05 billion in orders. Its debt priced at a 2.5-percentage-point spread, compared with 2.65 points when the existing bonds were first sold. Those outcomes indicated that recent concern about software-related private-credit valuations and limited fund redemptions had not closed public bond access for established managers.

Investors also showed interest in a more structured form of AI exposure. A Microsoft-linked data-center financing known as Project Odyssey attracted more than $8 billion of demand and could be increased to $3.9 billion, about $1 billion above the amount initially contemplated. The 5-year bonds, expected to carry investment-grade ratings, were being marketed with a high-6% coupon and a discounted issue price that would produce a low-to-mid-7% yield, closer to single-B junk debt than conventional high-grade paper.

The bonds would be issued by subsidiaries of Blackstone-backed QTS Realty Trust to finance a Georgia data-center venture. Long-term leases from hyperscalers can support investment-grade treatment, but the proposed yield shows investors demanding compensation for project structure, construction and concentration risk even when the ultimate tenant is Microsoft. The sale could reach the market as early as Tuesday, subject to change.

Alphabet is extending its funding program across currencies. The company was preparing its first Australian dollar bond offering, targeting about A$5 billion across four maturities extending to 20 years. It has already sold debt in US dollars, Swiss francs, sterling, euros, Canadian dollars and yen this year, alongside an equity offering of almost $85 billion. Its capital-spending forecast has risen to as much as $205 billion for 2026.

The Australian market offers both local diversification and a relative scarcity of technology issuers. That can support demand even as global investors show fatigue with the volume of hyperscaler borrowing. The distinction matters: buyers may resist another tightly priced dollar tranche after a record month while accepting a debut borrower that fills a gap in a local portfolio.

The AI financing cycle is affecting Treasury yields through more than bond supply. Spending on data centers, chips, power and labor has supported growth even as other parts of the economy soften. JPMorgan strategists expect infrastructure spending to total $5.5 trillion through 2030. That investment can keep real rates elevated through stronger demand while the associated borrowing absorbs the same capital that governments need to fund deficits.

## Japan’s Weak GDP Fails to Stop a JGB Rout

Japanese government bonds sold off even after Q2 growth disappointed, showing that currency pressure, inflation and fiscal uncertainty still outweigh weak domestic demand in the market’s near-term policy assessment. The 10-year JGB yield rose as much as 5.5 basis points to 2.93%, its highest since 1996. The 20-year climbed 6.5 basis points to 3.815%, while the 30-year increased 6 basis points to 4.07%, approaching its May record.

Real GDP expanded at a 1.1% annualized rate in Q2, short of the 2% median forecast and slower than the previous quarter’s revised 1.9%. The economy nevertheless grew for a third consecutive quarter. The weakness was concentrated in the domestic components the Bank of Japan would normally cite when judging whether demand can withstand higher rates.

Capital investment fell 1.2% from the previous quarter on a non-annualized basis, worse than the 0.5% increase economists expected and steeper than the revised 1% decline in Q1. Private consumption was unchanged, missing the forecast for a 0.4% gain, as higher living costs constrained household spending. The result contrasted with strong business surveys and industrial production, leaving a split between upbeat corporate sentiment and actual expenditure.

Inflation is central to that split. Corporate-goods prices rose 7.2% in July from a year earlier, increasing pressure on companies to pass higher fuel, material and imported costs to customers. Japan has diversified oil purchases as the Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed to normal traffic; the US supplied almost a third of its crude imports in June, up from 7% in February. The weaker yen magnifies those external costs.

The currency was around 159 per dollar after the GDP release, still far weaker than its 10-year average of 126.09 and close to levels that prompted coordinated US-Japan intervention in late July. Overnight swaps assigned roughly an 80% probability to a BOJ increase at the Sept. 18 meeting. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s government is supportive of a move in September or October, according to people familiar with the matter.

Weak GDP makes the rationale more difficult. A September increase would be harder to present as a response to overheating when consumption is flat and business investment is contracting. It could instead appear principally aimed at supporting the yen and limiting imported inflation. That does not preclude action, but it changes how investors may interpret the durability of the tightening cycle.

Former senior currency official Takehiko Nakao argued for a substantially faster path, saying the BOJ should increase rates at every meeting and eventually lift the policy rate above 2%. He said a rate of 2.25% or 2.5% would not be unusual with inflation around 2%, compared with the current 1% rate and still-negative real borrowing costs. His proposal is not BOJ guidance, but it illustrates the pressure from former currency officials who view monetary policy as necessary to reinforce intervention.

Fiscal policy adds another source of long-end risk. Takaichi plans to cut the sales tax on food to 1% for two years beginning in April, but the government has not explained how it will finance the measure. Household relief could support consumption after the weak Q2 result, while unfunded relief would add to concern about a public-debt burden already exceeding twice the size of the economy.

The Japanese selloff was part of a wider repricing of government debt. French 10-year yields remained near their highest since 2009, German yields traded around 2011 levels and Canada’s 30-year yield reached its highest since 2010. Across 32 swap markets, two-thirds were priced for higher rates, with about 400 basis points of combined increases expected across seven major markets over the next year.

The global picture is not uniform. Japan is weighing weak consumption against currency and import-price pressure, while Europe faces energy and defense spending and the US faces a large fiscal and corporate-duration burden. The common result is reduced protection from diversifying across sovereign markets when higher energy costs, fiscal expansion and AI investment are operating simultaneously.

## Liquidity and Growth Signals Diverge Across Emerging Markets

India delivered the sharpest sovereign-market reaction outside developed markets after the Reserve Bank of India said it would close a special dollar-deposit window for overseas residents at the end of August, one month earlier than scheduled. The announcement surprised traders because Governor Sanjay Malhotra had ruled out early termination at the Aug. 5 policy meeting.

The 5-year government yield rose as much as 9 basis points to 6.44%, while the 10-year climbed 4 basis points to 6.80%. The deposit facility had attracted more than $50 billion, and the associated inflows increased foreign-exchange reserves by over $30 billion in three weeks to $707 billion. Closing it early means less prospective rupee liquidity to support short-dated bonds.

The rupee weakened 0.2% to 95.58 per dollar. Citigroup reduced the level to which it thought the currency could strengthen in the near term to 95 from 94, while lowering its forecast for total gross facility inflows by $10 billion to $70 billion. The bank judged that engineering a large currency appreciation was not the RBI’s primary objective, even though the additional reserves give policymakers more capacity to limit volatility.

The RBI may also have concluded that further inflows offered diminishing benefits. The deposits carry maturities of three to five years, creating future foreign-currency liabilities, while the central bank bears the cost of forward premiums. Two other facilities for banks and state-owned companies remain open through December.

That distinction preserves an incentive for Indian lenders to issue offshore bonds. Financial institutions had already sold a record $8 billion of dollar debt this year, exceeding the previous full-year high of $7.92 billion in 2019. ICICI Bank was marketing another deal Monday, while Kotak Mahindra Bank and Yes Bank had appointed advisers for possible benchmark offerings.

The overseas-borrowing swap offers banks a fixed annual hedging rate of 1.5% for an average maturity of at least three years, below market cost. About two-thirds of Indian corporate dollar borrowing this year has come from financial institutions. The early end to the deposit program may accelerate issuance over the next several weeks even if volumes slow once the immediate funding need passes.

Brazil showed a different result of restrictive policy. The central bank’s economic-activity index fell 0.64% in June from the previous month, more than the 0.5% decline economists expected and the largest contraction since May 2025. Activity was still 2.35% higher than a year earlier, and the data indicated the economy expanded 0.2% in Q2 after growing 1.1% in Q1.

The central bank has lowered the Selic rate by 25 basis points at each of its past four meetings, bringing it to 14%, without committing to another move in September. Softer industrial production, services and inflation increase the case for further easing, but inflation remains above the 3% target and fiscal policy is keeping longer-term expectations elevated.

Finance Minister Dario Durigan acknowledged that investor concern about mandatory spending and public-debt dynamics is justified and said the government must address the trajectory. Inflation expectations remain above target through 2028, complicating the easing cycle even as current activity weakens. Durigan declined to endorse specific structural changes to pensions or spending rules, leaving the fiscal response unresolved ahead of the October election.

Elsewhere in Asia, Q2 Thai growth slowed to 1.9% from a year earlier, compared with 2.8% in Q1, although it exceeded the 1.8% forecast. Private investment rose 13.4%, the strongest increase since 2012, but higher energy costs and disrupted tourism weighed on domestic activity. The government raised the lower end of its full-year growth forecast, putting the range at 2%-2.5%, while high household debt and deteriorating small-business credit remain constraints.

China’s July data exposed a sharper divide between the AI-linked industrial economy and domestic demand. Industrial production rose 4.5% from a year earlier, retail-sales growth slowed to 0.6%, and fixed-asset investment fell 6.7% over the first seven months. All were weaker than expected. Electronic-equipment output rose more than 19%, but that strength was insufficient to offset the broader slowdown in consumption and investment.

Greece provided a constructive fiscal counterpoint. The government plans about €13 billion of early debt repayments in 2026, including roughly €2.5 billion of European Financial Stability Mechanism loans, a €2.2 billion bond due in 2027 and a €1.2 billion reduction in Treasury bills. The plan is not final, but strong primary surpluses and cash reserves expected to exceed €30 billion by year-end give Athens room to reduce future financing needs.

The debt agency expects the debt-to-GDP ratio to fall to 137% this year, below its prior forecast of 138.2%. The faster reduction has already helped Greece’s 10-year yield trade below those of Italy, France and the UK. The contrast with rising US and Japanese borrowing costs is less about the absolute size of Greece’s debt than the direction of its financing requirement and the credibility created by retiring obligations ahead of schedule.

## Corporate Access Coexists With Acute Borrower Stress

Record primary issuance did not prevent sharp repricing in individual credits. Sammons Financial Group’s June 2036 bonds fell to their lowest since issuance after a report examined the insurer’s connections to Guggenheim Partners and its chief executive, Mark Walter. The bonds widened to about 2 percentage points over their benchmark from 1.47 percentage points a week earlier.

The report’s publisher disclosed that its investment arm was short the bonds and cited filings describing Sammons as a related party to Guggenheim. Fitch had rated the insurer A- in June, citing very strong capital alongside modestly elevated exposure to riskier assets. Neither Sammons nor Guggenheim provided a response.

The concern was amplified by deterioration in Guggenheim’s own obligations as prosecutors and regulators examine loans made by Walter’s insurers to other parts of his business empire. Guggenheim’s first-lien term loan due in November 2031 was quoted below 80 cents on the dollar Monday, down from about par on July 20. The move introduced a borrower-specific counterpoint to otherwise strong demand for high-grade and private-credit-fund issuance.

In Brazil, Grupo Casas Bahia filed for court-supervised bankruptcy protection after an out-of-court restructuring initiated in 2024 failed to stabilize its finances. The retailer cited high rates, tight credit, rising funding costs, weak consumption and pressure on working capital. Its shares fell as much as 36% to a record low.

Local media reported 17.3 billion reais of liabilities. First-half revenue was 14.4 billion reais, while the net loss widened 18.4% from a year earlier to 11.2 billion reais. Casas Bahia closed 298 stores and reduced staff as it shifted toward more profitable operations, but planned liquidity-raising alternatives did not materialize. The company intends to keep its remaining sales channels operating while seeking longer debt maturities.

Braskem faces a separate Aug. 24 deadline to reach an out-of-court agreement or seek similar judicial protection. Petrobras is considering better commercial terms for the petrochemical producer, including longer payment periods, lower interest rates and increased naphtha supply. Petrobras’s share of Braskem’s naphtha supply has fallen to about 30% from as much as 70%, forcing Braskem to rely more heavily on other suppliers and bank credit.

No decision has been made. International bondholders have proposed terms that Braskem and some creditors view more favorably, but the company needs support from holders of at least one-third of its debt. Some creditors want Petrobras to provide equity, working capital or junior debt. The state-controlled oil company has resisted an equity injection that could increase its ownership and potentially consolidate Braskem’s obligations onto its own balance sheet.

Indonesian developer Modernland Realty is attempting its second restructuring of a $274.5 million dollar bond due next April. It proposes extending the maturity to June 30, 2028, before ultimately exchanging the debt for perpetual securities backed by assets transferred to a creditor-controlled vehicle.

Bondholders would receive an upfront payment of $50 for each $1,000 of principal. The amended notes would accrue 3% annual payment-in-kind interest, and unpaid interest before effectiveness would be capitalized. Part of the collateral would be released so Modernland could pledge those assets for a new $34 million facility. Creditors face an Aug. 24 voting deadline under a proposed pre-packaged Singapore scheme.

Riverside Military Academy obtained a longer reprieve after defaulting on roughly $48 million of municipal bonds. A forbearance agreement runs through Aug. 31, 2027, and the school will use a junior $8 million loan to provide bondholders with payments missed since March 2025. Enrollment had fallen almost 65% from 509 students in 2019 to 180 in 2024, weakening the operating base behind the debt.

These cases distinguish market access from credit repair. High-grade issuers and established private-credit funds can still expand deals when they offer sufficient spread, while distressed borrowers are relying on maturity extensions, payment-in-kind interest, junior capital and court protection. High benchmark yields intensify both outcomes: they attract capital to strong new issues and make refinancing more difficult for companies whose operations have already deteriorated.

## Forward Market Significance

Minutes from the Fed’s July meeting on Wednesday will provide the next test of the widening gap between policy expectations and long-term yields. Officials voted 9-3 to leave rates unchanged, but the summary may show whether the hold was closer than the vote suggests and how broadly policymakers shared concern about persistent goods inflation before the latest softer employment, retail and price reports.

A discussion emphasizing patience would support Goldman’s judgment that a September increase is unlikely and leave the long end to trade principally on supply, fiscal policy and real yields. Greater concern about more than half of core goods prices still rising would strengthen Citadel’s argument that September remains a close decision and could bring the 2-year more fully into the selloff.

Treasury’s 20-year auction this week will directly test demand after the 30-year yield reached a new cycle high. The relevant question is whether the latest concession attracts durable buying while corporate borrowers are offering large spreads and a heavy investment-grade calendar. A weak result would add another supply signal to the curve steepening; a firm award and stable secondary trading would show that yields above 5% are beginning to clear duration.

Oil remains the most immediate inflation risk. Trump’s refusal to extend the agreement with Iran and renewed fighting in Lebanon pushed Brent above $91, but producers have continued moving crude through alternative transfers around the Strait of Hormuz. Sustained volumes and lower freight or insurance costs would contain the economic effect even without a diplomatic settlement. Disrupted transfers, tighter enforcement around Iranian ports or further attacks would increase the risk that higher energy prices enter inflation expectations and central-bank pricing.

UK inflation on Wednesday is expected to rise 2.9% from a year earlier, its first acceleration in four months. Energy bills, air travel and shortages of AI-related electronic components are expected to contribute. The result will test whether the Bank of England can distinguish imported and sector-specific pressure from a broader domestic inflation impulse.

Friday’s global purchasing-manager surveys are the next broad activity check after weaker releases from Japan, China, Thailand and Brazil. US data strong enough to preserve the country’s growth advantage could revive the dollar and complicate the reduction in Fed wagers. Further weakness would reinforce patience at the front end but would not necessarily lower long yields if corporate borrowing and fiscal supply remain heavy.

In Japan, the Sept. 18 BOJ meeting now carries a more difficult mix of evidence. An 80% market-implied probability of an increase, a yen near 159 and 7.2% corporate-goods inflation favor action, while 1.1% annualized GDP growth, flat consumption and falling investment argue against an aggressive sequence. Guidance on whether one increase is intended to stabilize the currency or begins a faster normalization path will matter at least as much as the first move.

Primary credit markets face immediate execution tests. Project Odyssey could bring its enlarged Microsoft-linked financing as soon as Tuesday, while Alphabet is expected to provide price guidance for its four-part Australian dollar debut before possible pricing the following day. The concessions needed to complete those deals will indicate whether scarcity in local currencies and high project yields can overcome the fatigue visible in recent US order attrition.

The Aug. 24 deadlines for Modernland and Braskem pose a different question. Modernland must secure approval for a restructuring that exchanges maturity relief and new collateral flexibility for payment-in-kind interest and an eventual perpetual security. Braskem needs support from at least one-third of creditors while determining whether Petrobras will provide commercial relief without assuming a larger balance-sheet obligation. In both cases, the operative market test is the allocation of new money, collateral and losses, not merely whether talks continue.

Rising real yields, federal deficits and record AI-related corporate borrowing drove the steepening, while renewed oil risk added an inflation threat without materially lifting the 10-year breakeven.

section_summaries.market_read: Treasuries must clear at yields attractive relative to corporate debt offering additional spread and, in some cases, long leases.
section_summaries.section_title: Long-Duration Supply Overrides the Softer Fed Path
section_summaries.summary: The 30-year yield rose 4.7 basis points while the 5-year added 1 basis point, extending a one-month selloff concentrated at the long end. Heavy corporate duration, fiscal borrowing and more price-sensitive private demand forced Treasuries to compete with highly rated bonds offering substantial concessions.

section_summaries.market_read: AI investment can keep real rates elevated through stronger demand while its borrowing absorbs capital also needed by governments.
section_summaries.next_check: Project Odyssey may launch Tuesday, with Alphabet’s Australian dollar debut potentially pricing the following day.
section_summaries.section_title: AI Borrowing Sets Another Primary-Market Record
section_summaries.summary: August investment-grade issuance reached a record $145.2 billion, led by Alphabet’s $25 billion deal, as technology borrowers funded a widening AI buildout. Demand remained available but more selective, supporting enlarged private-credit and data-center financings while requiring meaningful concessions.

section_summaries.market_read: Weak growth complicates the rationale for tightening but does not remove currency, import-price or fiscal pressure from long yields.
section_summaries.next_check: The Sept. 18 BOJ decision must clarify whether an increase is currency support or the start of faster normalization.
section_summaries.section_title: Japan’s Weak GDP Fails to Stop a JGB Rout
section_summaries.summary: JGBs sold off despite Q2 growth of only 1.1% annualized as a weak yen, 7.2% corporate-goods inflation and fiscal uncertainty outweighed flat consumption and falling investment. The tension makes any BOJ increase look partly aimed at limiting imported inflation rather than cooling domestic demand.

section_summaries.section_title: Liquidity and Growth Signals Diverge Across Emerging Markets
section_summaries.summary: India’s early closure of a special dollar-deposit window reduced expected rupee liquidity and lifted government yields, while its remaining offshore-borrowing incentive may accelerate bank issuance. Brazil’s activity contraction strengthened the case for easing but unresolved fiscal risk constrained the path; China and Thailand also showed uneven growth, while Greece planned early debt repayments.

section_summaries.market_read: High benchmark yields attract capital to well-priced new issues while making refinancing harder for borrowers with weak operations.
section_summaries.next_check: Braskem and Modernland face Aug. 24 deadlines to secure creditor support and determine the allocation of new money and losses.
section_summaries.section_title: Corporate Access Coexists With Acute Borrower Stress
section_summaries.summary: Strong primary demand coexisted with acute borrower stress. Sammons and Guggenheim obligations repriced sharply, Casas Bahia sought court protection, and Braskem and Modernland pursued creditor relief, showing that access remained open for stronger issuers while weaker borrowers depended on extensions, junior capital and restructuring.

Fed minutes will test whether softer policy expectations can survive concern about persistent goods inflation, while the 20-year Treasury auction will show whether yields above 5% can attract durable demand amid heavy corporate supply. Oil-transfer conditions remain the nearest risk to inflation expectations and central-bank pricing.

overall_summary.headline: Treasury curve steepens as fiscal and record AI borrowing pressures outweigh a softer Fed path
overall_summary.session_narrative:
The Treasury curve steepened as long-duration financing pressure outweighed reduced expectations for a near-term Fed increase. The 30-year yield rose 4.7 basis points to 5.308%, its highest since 2007, while the 10-year gained 3 basis points to 4.723% and the 2-year added just 0.6 basis point. Nearly all of the 10-year move came from a 2.8-basis-point rise in the real yield, with the breakeven up only 0.2 basis point.

August investment-grade issuance reached a record $145.2 billion as AI investment added corporate duration to a market already financing annual federal deficits near $2 trillion. Technology borrowers have sold roughly $200 billion this year, and their concessions over government debt are encouraging investors to shift capital from Treasuries. Oil added inflation risk after the US-Iran negotiating window was not extended, though alternative transfers around the Strait of Hormuz continued to limit physical disruption.

Weaker employment, retail-sales and inflation data pushed the expected timing of the next Fed increase to January, weighing on the dollar and limiting the front-end selloff. Risk assets remained divided: semiconductor shares gained on AI demand, but broader equities fell and volatility rose as the financing burden of that investment cycle pressured other assets.
overall_summary.summary: Long Treasury yields climbed and the curve steepened as deficits, heavy AI-linked corporate issuance and renewed oil risk raised duration costs, while weaker data pushed expectations for the next Fed increase into January and kept the 2-year move small.
